review.notes: No way in is marked and the evidence does not say which is most used; the three ways overlap and the route name pairs Switchback with Klahhane Ridge. Skipped.

problems: No primary marked and evidence is split between the Hurricane Ridge climbers' trail and the Switchback Trail start; owner to choose.

why.Boulder Creek from the Elwha: When coming from the Elwha side or making Boulder Lake a camp, though the closed road below the trailhead makes it the longer way in.

review.notes: Both sides reach Appleton Pass; the Elwha side carries a road walk. No route-specific page found for the peak itself.

why.South Fork Slate Creek and the east ridg: When a shorter, less brushy approach with clearer route-finding is wanted and the Slate Creek road is passable; snow in the upper cirque speeds travel.
why.West Fork Methow and the PCT: On a combined trip with neighbouring peaks, since the trail and Pacific Crest Trail avoid the overgrown Mill Creek tread at the cost of extra mileage.

review.notes: Reports describe the Slate Creek east side as the usual standard route and the Mill Creek trail as very poor, which conflicts with the marked primary. Mark left unchanged.
fromStoredNotes: West Fork Methow and the PCT

problems: The marked primary (Mill Creek / Azurite Pass) conflicts with stored notes and trip reports saying the Slate Creek east side is what most parties use; owner to decide.

why.Up the Elwha to Elwha Basin: When approaching from the Elwha side rather than traversing the Bailey crest from the Sol Duc, accepting a several-day walk and possibly a long road walk at the start.

review.notes: Elwha Basin is a recognised entry to the Bailey Range; no detailed summit-route page found.
fromStoredNotes: Up the Elwha to Elwha Basin

why.Trinity and Buck Creek, or the High Pass: When the unbridged Chiwawa ford at Little Giant is too high to cross; the High Pass line is longer but has the least off-trail travel.

review.notes: Search describes Buck Creek Pass and High Pass as the easiest and most common general access, while Little Giant is the shortest. Mark left unchanged.

problems: Search describes the Buck Creek Pass / High Pass access as the easiest and most common, whereas the marked primary is the Little Giant route; owner may wish to check.

why.Horsehead Pass and the west slopes: When snow still fills the notch above the upper lake or the cliff-band route-finding is unwanted; a longer, looser walk-up from the west.

review.notes: West slopes via Horsehead Pass confirmed as the easy route to the summit.

why.Kindy Ridge from the Kindy Creek road: When coming from the Cascade River side, or when the Suiattle River Road is closed; a longer two to three day approach.

review.notes: Green Mountain is described as the shortest approach, consistent with the marked primary. No page found detailing the Kindy Creek approach.
fromStoredNotes: Kindy Ridge from the Kindy Creek road

why.Deer Park and the Cameron Creek Trail: When Obstruction Point Road is still closed; longer, with little-maintained tread and heavy brush, but it joins the same route at Cameron Pass.
why.Dosewallips road walk and the long push: Rarely used now; mostly for parties already on a Dosewallips valley trip, since the closed road adds many miles over either northern approach.

review.notes: Obstruction Point and Grand Pass confirmed as the usual northern entry; Cameron Creek is reached via Deer Park or Grand Pass.
fromStoredNotes: Dosewallips road walk and the long push up-valley into Cameron Basin

review.notes: Slate Pass is confirmed as the shortest approach (about 15 miles); Monument Creek is longer. The non-primary entry is a climbing gully with an approach paragraph, not a distinct way in, so no honest reason could be written.

problems: The way in 'The south gully below the Carru-Lago col' describes the climb and both approaches, not a separate approach; it should probably be split or reworded (Monument Creek is the real alternative).

why.Hannegan Pass, Chilliwack River and What: When snow makes the Impasse on Easy Ridge impassable or wet; it trades that for a glacier traverse around Whatcom Peak, a late-season problem in low-snow years.

review.notes: Easy Ridge to Perfect Pass is the most common approach; the Impasse is its crux.

why.Elwha side to Low Divide, from Whiskey B: When approaching from the Elwha or linking a longer trip across Low Divide; the Whiskey Bend closure adds a long road walk each way, which keeps it uncommon.

review.notes: Low Divide is reached from either river; the Quinault side is the usual one.
fromStoredNotes: Elwha side to Low Divide, from Whiskey Bend

why.Bike the closed Dosewallips roadbed: To cut the long road walk at both ends of the trip, leaving the bike at the start of the climbers' path; the climb above is the same.

review.notes: Biking the roadbed is widely recommended and used, so it may be as common as walking.

problems: Search reports describe biking the roadbed as highly recommended and common; the walk-in being primary may be questionable.
